abstract_draft: Continuous-action vision-language-action policies can execute an action successfully in one scene yet fail after a small geometry edit that leaves the task and most of the trajectory unchanged. Recent work adds explicit feasibility supervision [semanticscholar:dd324415c99589f1f7f9b63eaa3a64a7ae042df2], geometry-guided action manifolds [semanticscholar:8cb14cd9dafae88163a7685336a02ac6c41ed646], or geometry-aware representations [dblp:journals/corr/abs-2606-08530], but their aggregate objectives do not identify where feasibility first flips or whether suppressing the invalid action erases other valid modes. We propose Boundary-Local Score Matching (BLSM): compile same-action minimal geometry flips, certify the first contiguous violation segment, apply a reference-adjusted feasible-versus-invalid score preference only on that segment, anchor scores on its complement, and preserve every compiler-enumerated feasible alternative independently. The proposal is falsified if violation-mask or pair-identity permutations retain the edited-scene and mode-coverage gains, or if removing alternative-positive preservation leaves worst-mode success unchanged when coverage is already high. Conditional on non-negligible pair eligibility and mode-roster support, BLSM should increase edited-scene success and reduce invalid execution without the alternative-positive coverage loss induced by global or whole-chunk feasibility shaping. The intended contribution is therefore a mechanism-level sign split between physical reliability and per-mode retention, rather than another average-success improvement.
motivation.problem_framing:
Functional geometry changes define a structural problem class in which the instruction, manipulated objects, and much of a candidate action remain stable while a small change in clearance, pose, or contact geometry changes the feasible action set. A continuous-action VLA trained by ordinary imitation receives no direct signal about that decision boundary. Global feasibility supervision can reject an invalid rollout, but it spreads credit over an entire action chunk and can depress nearby actions that remain physically valid. The core bottleneck is therefore not merely recognizing geometry; it is assigning a feasibility change to the first trajectory segment that actually violates the edited scene while retaining the other valid modes.

The closest adjacent systems address pieces of this structure but leave the credit-and-retention question unresolved. Explicit feasibility supervision targets invalid actions [semanticscholar:dd324415c99589f1f7f9b63eaa3a64a7ae042df2], Action Manifold Learning constrains prediction to geometry-guided valid regions [semanticscholar:8cb14cd9dafae88163a7685336a02ac6c41ed646], KeyStone selects a dominant consistent action cluster [semanticscholar:4a71dc5d2b6b4ea2a6477ec4515d8294e3c75383], GEAR-VLA aligns geometry-aware representations [dblp:journals/corr/abs-2606-08530], and STARRY couples future spatial-temporal latents to actions [semanticscholar:f134eaaeb2cf6d4ac3526993199033b7f858a35b]. None of the available records establishes a matched minimal edit, first-violation credit mask, complement-drift constraint, and mode-wise retention target in one mechanism. BLSM turns that residue into an identifiable training object: the score change that should occur at a certified feasibility boundary, separated from the score changes that should not occur elsewhere.
motivation.why_now: The gap is timely because recent VLA work has made geometry and continuous-action structure explicit enough to support controlled boundary construction: Pointing-VLA exposes typed spatial grounding [semanticscholar:aaef4e8a3bd4a3a4f6673b2d4bce0a3237783cb9], WNM-3D maintains persistent 3D context [semanticscholar:74257100ad8c273b90dbaaba190e1f699ec9df0a], Action Manifold Learning supplies a geometry-guided validity view [semanticscholar:8cb14cd9dafae88163a7685336a02ac6c41ed646], and KeyStone makes action-mode structure measurable [semanticscholar:4a71dc5d2b6b4ea2a6477ec4515d8294e3c75383]. Together with scripted RoboTwin 2.0 scene edits and a frozen continuous-action reference policy, these ingredients permit paired counterfactuals, simulator-certified violation masks, and per-mode score accounting that earlier aggregate feasibility objectives could not expose.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[0].what_the: Can Explicit Physical Feasibility Benefit VLA Learning? studies a geometry-grounded feasibility objective for suppressing physically invalid robot actions.
Its available abstract does not establish same-action minimum geometry flips, first-violation-local score credit, complement anchoring, or independent retention of every feasible alternative mode.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[0].structur: The missing ingredient is a paired boundary-construction and temporal-localization instrument; full-text absence also prevents verifying whether any equivalent mechanism is present.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[1].what_the: Learning Action Manifold with Multi-view Latent Priors predicts actions on a geometry-guided valid manifold to reduce monocular ambiguity and inefficient regression.
It does not use a minimal geometry intervention to measure which formerly valid mode becomes invalid or explicitly preserve worst-case retention across the remaining valid modes.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[1].structur: Its representation-level manifold objective lacks the paired score-change estimand and mode-indexed preservation mechanism required for boundary-local credit.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[2].what_the: Geometry Guided Self-Consistency for Physical AI samples candidate actions and executes the medoid of the largest geometry-consistent cluster.
It does not treat minority feasible clusters as protected positives or test whether feasibility shaping preserves each alternative mode after a geometry flip.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[2].structur: Largest-cluster aggregation removes mode identity from the objective, so it has no measurement or loss term for compiler-relative worst-mode retention.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[3].what_the: GEAR-VLA aligns 3D features and learns a canonicalized continuous-action expert for more generalizable manipulation.
It does not construct identical-action feasibility flips, localize the first violating segment, or separate necessary local score change from unwanted complement drift.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[3].structur: Its primary object is geometry-aware representation transfer rather than an interventional temporal credit signal with matched retention diagnostics.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[4].what_the: STARRY jointly denoises future spatial-temporal latents and actions through depth-conditioned attention for manipulation.
It does not estimate a reference-adjusted margin from a controlled validity flip or constrain action-score drift outside the simulator-certified violation segment.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[4].structur: Joint future-and-action denoising supplies no matched counterfactual boundary label or unique decomposition-derived supervisory signal.
motivation.what_changes_when_gap_closes: Closing this gap would let a VLA learn that a particular contact or clearance segment must change after a geometry edit while retaining all other feasible ways to finish the task. It would also make the reliability-diversity trade-off measurable: feasibility methods such as [semanticscholar:dd324415c99589f1f7f9b63eaa3a64a7ae042df2] and geometry-guided action methods such as [semanticscholar:8cb14cd9dafae88163a7685336a02ac6c41ed646] could be judged not only by invalid-action suppression, but by complement drift, alternative-positive coverage, and worst-mode success.
core_claim: On same-action minimal geometry flips, first-violation-local reference-adjusted score shaping with complement and alternative-mode anchoring can suppress invalid execution without the feasible-mode coverage loss caused by global or whole-chunk shaping.

sub_claims.statement: A minimum feasibility-flipping scene edit holding task and action identity fixed isolates a functional-geometry boundary rather than a generic scene-distribution shift.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Identifiability of the geometry-induced feasibility bottleneck

sub_claims.statement: A simulator-certified first-violation mask assigns the feasible-versus-invalid score preference only where the edited geometry first changes execution validity, while complement anchoring limits unrelated score drift.
Mode-wise anchoring of every compiler-enumerated feasible alternative prevents the local negative signal from collapsing minority valid modes.
Pair-eligibility gates and mask, identity, and preservation interventions distinguish the proposed boundary mechanism from generic extra supervision or selected-subset effects.

key_equations.latex: \Delta g^*=\arg\min_{\Delta g} C(\Delta g)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad F(x,a^-)=1,\;F(x\oplus\Delta g,a^-)=0
key_equations.description: The compiler chooses the lowest-cost geometry edit that flips the identical action chunk from feasible to infeasible.
key_equations.description_zh: 编译器寻找代价最小的几何改动，使同一动作片段从可行变为不可行。

key_equations.description: The mask is the first contiguous simulator-certified violation run beginning at the earliest violating time τ.
key_equations.description_zh: 掩码取从最早违规时刻 τ 开始、由模拟器确认的首个连续违规区间。

key_equations.description: Every action score is expressed as a change from the frozen reference policy, preventing raw score scale from defining the preference.
key_equations.description_zh: 动作得分以相对冻结参考策略的变化量表示，避免原始得分尺度主导偏好。

key_equations.latex: d_\theta^{(k)}=\frac{\sum_t m_t[\Delta_\theta(a^+_{k,t}\mid x')-\Delta_\theta(a^-_t\mid x')]}{\sum_t m_t},\quad \mathcal{L}_B=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\log(1+e^{-d_\theta^{(k)}}),\quad M_B=\mathbb{E}[d_\theta]
key_equations.description: The boundary loss increases the masked reference-adjusted margin of each feasible alternative over the invalid action; M_B is the held-out mean margin.
key_equations.description_zh: 边界损失提升每个可行替代动作相对无效动作的掩码参考校正间隔；M_B 是留出数据上的平均间隔。

key_equations.description: Complement anchoring limits off-boundary drift, while the equally weighted alternative loss anchors every feasible mode rather than only the dominant one.
key_equations.description_zh: 补集锚定限制边界外漂移；等权替代项逐一保护所有可行模式，而非只保护主导模式。

key_equations.description: BLSM adds boundary preference, complement stability, and mode preservation to the ordinary imitation objective; the three weights are selected once on validation pairs and then frozen.
key_equations.description_zh: BLSM 在常规模仿目标上加入边界偏好、补集稳定与模式保护；三个权重在验证对上一次选定后固定。

method_flow.high_level_pipeline: BLSM starts from successful RoboTwin action chunks and compiles the smallest scene-geometry edits that make the identical chunk invalid while preserving the task. Simulator replay identifies the first contiguous violation segment and enumerates the feasible alternative-action roster in the edited scene. A frozen reference policy converts candidate scores into score changes; training then prefers each feasible alternative over the invalid chunk only inside the violation mask, anchors the mask complement, and separately anchors every feasible mode. The resulting post-trained policy is characterized by its held-out boundary margin, edited-scene validity, complement drift, alternative-positive coverage, and worst-mode retention.

method_flow.steps.title: Compile minimal feasibility flips
method_flow.steps.what_changes: For each frozen-policy action chunk that succeeds in an original RoboTwin 2.0 scene, search the scene compiler over task-preserving geometry edits and retain the minimum-cost edit that makes the identical chunk fail; record every attempted pair and its inclusion or exclusion reason.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: Holding task and action identity fixed makes geometry-induced feasibility the only intended difference and exposes whether eligible boundary pairs occupy more than a selected corner of the data.
method_flow.steps.input: Original RoboTwin 2.0 scenes, task instructions, frozen-policy action chunks, and simulator feasibility checks
method_flow.steps.output: Accepted original/edited BoundaryFlip pairs plus a complete eligibility ledger

method_flow.steps.title: Certify the first violation run
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Replay the identical chunk in both scenes, compute the simulator violation indicator at each action time, and set m to the first contiguous violating run in the edited scene rather than labeling the full chunk.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: The decomposition is derived from observed simulator structure and yields the unique temporal region on which the geometry edit first changes functional validity.
method_flow.steps.input: An accepted BoundaryFlip pair and synchronized simulator traces
method_flow.steps.output: A nonempty first-violation mask m and its complement

method_flow.steps.title: Enumerate feasible alternative modes
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Run the same task compiler in the edited scene to enumerate feasible action chunks, partition them by the compiler's action-mode identity, and retain one scored roster entry for every supported mode rather than only the largest cluster.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: A mode-indexed roster makes positive coverage and worst-mode retention observable and prevents dominant-mode aggregation from hiding feasible alternatives.
method_flow.steps.input: Edited scene, task specification, and compiler-generated feasible solutions
method_flow.steps.output: Alternative-positive roster A+ with mode identities and roster-size metadata

method_flow.steps.title: Match boundary-local score changes
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Evaluate the trainable and frozen-reference action scores for the invalid chunk and each feasible alternative under the edited observation, form their reference-adjusted difference, and apply a feasible-over-invalid soft preference only at times selected by m.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: Reference adjustment isolates post-training movement, while mask-local preference directs feasibility credit to the segment implicated by the counterfactual rather than the whole action chunk.
method_flow.steps.input: Violation mask, invalid action chunk, alternative-positive roster, edited observation, and frozen reference policy
method_flow.steps.output: Boundary preference loss L_B and per-mode margins d_theta

method_flow.steps.title: Anchor the complement and every positive
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Penalize reference-adjusted score drift outside m for all rostered chunks and add an equal-per-mode score anchor for every feasible alternative, without pooling alternatives by frequency.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: The complement term prevents temporal credit leakage, and the alternative term makes suppression of minority feasible modes costly even when average validity improves.
method_flow.steps.input: Reference-adjusted scores, mask complement, and the full alternative-positive roster
method_flow.steps.output: Complement loss L_comp and alternative-preservation loss L_alt

method_flow.steps.title: Optimize and expose the boundary diagnostics
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Add L_B, L_comp, and L_alt to ordinary imitation, select their symbolic weights on validation pairs by first preventing complement and worst-mode degradation and then improving boundary separation, freeze the selected weights, and report M_B together with eligibility, mask-length, roster-size, drift, coverage, and worst-mode summaries.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: A constrained selection rule prevents an arbitrary loss-weight trade-off from masquerading as the mechanism, while the exposed diagnostics connect score movement to downstream reliability and retention.
method_flow.steps.input: Imitation batches and the three BLSM loss terms
method_flow.steps.output: A post-trained continuous-action VLA and boundary-mechanism diagnostics

method_flow.design_reasoning_echo: The design assumes that the simulator's feasibility predicate is correct for the task, the compiler's accepted edit is sufficiently minimal to isolate functional geometry, the first contiguous violation run captures the earliest operative failure, and the enumerated roster represents the feasible alternatives; each premise is exposed through eligibility, mask-length, roster-size, and exclusion reports rather than hidden in preprocessing. The observation model is conditional on compiler-attempted simulator pairs, so the estimand is the held-out reference-adjusted feasible-versus-invalid score margin at an accepted geometry boundary, not an unrestricted real-world causal effect. A naive global feasibility loss can suppress the invalid chunk but cannot say where the score should change and can lower nearby valid modes. BLSM therefore couples the decomposition-derived boundary preference with the two invariances implied by that decomposition: little score movement off the boundary and no mode-wise loss on feasible alternatives. Mask and identity permutations, plus removal of the alternative anchor, directly test whether these components—not generic extra supervision—produce the downstream sign split.
feasibility_validation.data.rationale: RoboTwin 2.0 scenes, scripted geometry edits, simulator traces, and continuous-action policy rollouts are nameable accessible sources, and the required positive rosters can be generated by the same task compiler.
feasibility_validation.theoretical.ratio: No theorem is load-bearing; the equations define an empirical score-shaping objective and identifiable diagnostics rather than a formal theoretical contribution.
feasibility_validation.engineering.ratio: The binding implementation cost is robust minimum-edit search plus synchronized first-violation and mode-roster extraction across many simulator pairs, although each component is scriptable with existing RoboTwin tooling.
feasibility_validation.falsification.rat: The held-out boundary margin, mask and identity permutations, alternative-anchor removal, and downstream validity and retention metrics are concrete interventions measurable with the same simulator and score interface.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses[0].respo: The defense is anchored in method steps S1-S5 and the locked falsification prediction: the claimed delta is the conjunction of same-action minimum edits, first-violation localization, complement anchoring, and compiler-relative worst-mode preservation, not the broad use of feasibility supervision. Because the threatening paper is available only at abstract level, this remains a conditional distinction; full-text verification must show that it does not already implement that conjunction.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses[1].respo: A targeted scoop-check must establish that the feasibility-weighting or local-credit family does not already combine minimum same-action geometry flips, reference-adjusted first-violation preference, complement-drift control, and mode-wise positive preservation. Finding that joint mechanism would remove the candidate's novelty delta even if its terminology differs.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses[2].respo: The decomposition in S2 is not a sensitivity or redundancy proxy: it is the first simulator-certified violation run induced by the minimum functional-geometry edit, and S4-S5 assign the distinct treatments uniquely implied by boundary membership. The heterogeneity is therefore explained by where execution validity first changes, while the complement and per-mode anchors make the proposal more than a bundle of generic compression or calibration components.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses[3].respo: The diagnostic does more than reconfirm that geometry matters: it measures the previously conflated sign split between invalid-action suppression and retention of each still-feasible action mode. The eligibility ledger, held-out task and geometry families, frozen-policy outcomes for exclusions, and mask or pair-identity permutations reduce selection and definitional circularity; transfer beyond RoboTwin remains an open ecological-validity limit rather than a claimed result.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses[4].respo: S2 derives the decomposition from the observed first simulator-certified violation run under a task-preserving geometry flip, and S4 manufactures exactly the corresponding masked preference while S5 anchors the implied complement. The locked falsification prediction separates decomposition from signal by permuting masks or pair identities and tests the independent preservation mechanism through L_alt removal, so a gain that survives those interventions does not support the proposed explanation.
domain_landscape.position_note: BLSM combines a saturated heterogeneous-decomposition pattern (9 of 18 papers) with the scarcely used controlled-diagnostic pattern (1 of 18), using the former for boundary-local treatment and the latter to expose its reliability-versus-mode-retention consequence.
